en: Vimānavatthu:
Itthivimāna, Cittalatāvagga (The Chapter on the Cittalatā Grove)
7. The Mansion of the Uposatha Deity “O deity,
with such surpassing beauty with which you stand there— ”
Illuminating all directions like a star among the herbs—
by what means do you possess such a complexion?
"...and your beauty illuminates all directions.
That deity was uplifted in mind.
"They knew me as 'Uposatha,' the fruit of which action this is."
This laywoman of Sāketa is endowed with faith and virtue,
and she always delights in sharing.
I gave clothing, food, lodgings, and lamps to those who were upright.
With a serene mind,
on the fourteenth, the fifteenth,
and the eighth day of the lunar fortnight.
And during the fortnight of miracles,
I shall observe the Uposatha, perfectly endowed with its eight factors.
Always restrained in our virtue,
self-controlled and generous,
we now dwell in this celestial mansion.
Abstaining from taking life,
restrained from false speech,
and from theft and sexual misconduct,
And far removed from the drinking of intoxicants;
delighting in the five precepts,
they are skilled in the Noble Truths.
I am a female lay follower of Gotama, the illustrious one who possesses the eye;
because of that, my complexion is such as this.

A desire arose within me;
having directed my mind toward that,
I was reborn in Nandana.
I did not heed the word of the Teacher,
the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun;
having fixed my mind upon what is inferior, I failed to follow his instruction.
“I am one who later regrets.
“How long will you remain here in this celestial palace on the auspicious Uposatha day?”
“O deity, being asked,
tell me if you know [the duration] of life.
“Sixty thousand years,” [he replied].
And for thirty million years;
having stayed here, O Great Sage,
when I pass away from this life, I shall go [to heaven].
“Do not fear the Uposatha day; you have been declared by the Fully Awakened One to be destined for companionship with human beings.”
“Having become stream-enterers, you have distinguished yourself;
your miserable rebirths have been abandoned.
The seventh Vimāna, Uposatha.
